title: Embedded oversized tool-call JSON is silently ignored instead of rejected
reasoning: The parser advertises max JSON size enforcement as part of the LLM response trust boundary, and pure JSON responses over max_json_size raise InputSizeLimitError. Embedded JSON takes a different path: when an embedded JSON object exceeds max_json_size, parse_embedded_json just advances the scan position and continues. A model can therefore include an oversized tool-call-shaped JSON object inside surrounding text and have it treated as conversational content, bypassing the hard-error behavior and metrics used for pure JSON.
reproduction: Configure max_json_size smaller than an embedded JSON object that contains a functionCall, then parse a response like `prefix {"functionCall":{"name":"read_file","args":{"payload":"...large..."}}} suffix`. The embedded path skips the object instead of raising the same size-limit error as parse_json_response.
recommendation: Make embedded JSON size violations raise InputSizeLimitError and record the size violation when the decoded JSON object exceeds max_json_size, at least when the object has the configured tool-call root key. If deliberately ignoring non-tool JSON is required, inspect only enough to distinguish tool-call-shaped payloads before deciding whether to raise.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included extraction tests cover the max_response_size scan boundary and a small valid JSON object followed by large trailing text, but there is no test for an embedded tool-call JSON object whose own size exceeds max_json_size.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a parser_extraction test with low max_json_size and an embedded functionCall object larger than the limit; assert InputSizeLimitError and a size-violation metric rather than an empty tool call list.
minimumFixScope: Update JsonToolCallExtractor.parse_embedded_json oversized-object handling and add focused parser_extraction coverage.
